There's nothing wrong in principle about self-censorship, in theory it's no different than not telling someone in real life that they're a retard when they make a stupid comment, the issue is that things get a bit more gray when you bring money into the situation. It becomes hard to tell if they are censoring themselves because they want to or because they believe they'll make more money by doing it (to what degree varies), and it becomes even worse when one can argue that they aren't making anymore money by doing it. The issue here is that I imagine he's trying to add a bit more nuance into the discussion, for simplicities sake we often just say 'censorship' when companies choose to remove something or not do something that we at least perceive to be the result of them trying to appease a very vocal group of people that we believe they shouldn't be bending over backwards for, and I feel that both adding nuance and simplifying things serve purposes, simplifying helps get more people to talk because let's face it, most of us don't exactly think that it's worth spending hours writing out our ideas in great detail (heck even though I sometimes do it I often tire myself out just by talking so much when I do) so simplifying discussion makes it easier for us to communicate ideas, get more people involved, and generally gloss over facts that we for the most part agree on, but conversely by simplifying discussion some people are left blind to the nuance if only because the idea that sometimes censorship (like maybe not shouting fire in a crowded building) is sometimes 'alright' doesn't cross their mind, these people are then left only seeing part of a picture and perhaps have more extreme emotional reactions and all as a result, something which can serve to hinder discussion as you have to walk on egg-shells in order to explain the nuance without eliciting a rage-fueled backlash. So in terms of general talk on self-censorship I don't think there's anything wrong with what he's said, he's just trying to add some more nuance into a simplified discussion, and since both serve a purpose I personally don't think there's a point in really getting worked on on any measure of simplification or nuance as long as they are not demonstrably wrong (not being the whole story is merely an argument that there's not ENOUGH nuance, not that we need less).

That said, I do feel that perhaps some things are overlooked with the specific example he brings up, one thing being that this happened while we're still a little sore after the whole DoAX3 thing, region specific censorship does NOT reflect the views of the person who made it purely giving into outcry, and from what I heard the butt-slap thing is region specific which if true would sink the entire argument that the people in charge changed their mind, if these Japanese based companies had a problem with it, it would be removed from the Japanese version, but if it's not region specific then that in turn shoots down the argument that it was done due to SJWs I do believe, as if these companies were censoring only for them then the Japanese version of these games would remain unchanged given how these sorts of outcries generally don't have an effect on Japanese culture. That said though, even if the butt-slap isn't region specific I can still understand why some people might think that it is, because simply speaking again this happened not that long after the DoAX3 thing, which has left people a lot more sensitive to region specific censorship so I can understand, even if I don't agree, with people reacting as if something that isn't region specific censorship is, and from what I've seen that's the outcry that has been going on which I don't really disagree with aside from perhaps the more mob mentality that the outcry being on the internet lends itself to.

But those are just my thoughts.

I only skimmed the second half, but I saw nothing I strongly disagree with. The real line comes when people aren't self censoring due to their own beliefs, opinions, or even market forces (some folks aren't trying to make a statement, just a buck), but due to pressure from people who without the effort to pressure would otherwise not be involved at all. That is where it transforms from self censorship to being censored.
